assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Convection current
items.clue: Warm, less dense fluid rises, cools, becomes denser and sinks.

items.label: Black body
items.clue: Absorbs all the radiation falling on it and is the best possible emitter.

items.label: Conduction
items.clue: Transfer of thermal energy through a material without bulk movement of the material.

items.label: Luminosity L
items.clue: The total power emitted as electromagnetic radiation by a body over its whole surface.

questions.stem: A pure substance is heated steadily from a solid until it has completely boiled. According to the molecular model, which statement about its molecules is correct?

options.text: Their mean separation increases greatly on melting and increases again on boiling.
Their mean separation changes little on melting but increases greatly on boiling.
The molecules themselves get larger on melting, and larger again on boiling.
The molecules start to move only on melting, and they move faster still on boiling.

questions.explanation: In a solid and a liquid the molecules are close together, which is why their densities are similar; melting frees them from fixed positions without separating them much. On boiling they move far apart: the gas is roughly a thousand times less dense than the liquid.

questions.stem: The density of aluminium is 2.7 g cm⁻³. What is the volume, in m³, of an aluminium block of mass 0.081 kg?
questions.explanation: ρ = m/V, so V = m/ρ = 81 g/2.7 g cm⁻³ = 30 cm³. Since 1 cm³ = (10⁻² m)³ = 10⁻⁶ m³, V = 30 × 10⁻⁶ m³ = 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ m³. (In SI: V = 0.081 kg/2700 kg m⁻³ gives the same result.)

questions.stem: Liquefied natural gas is stored at 112 K, the boiling point of methane at atmospheric pressure. What is this temperature on the Celsius scale?
questions.explanation: θ/°C = T/K − 273 = 112 − 273 = −161 °C. A temperature below 273 K is below the melting point of ice, so it must be negative on the Celsius scale.

questions.stem: At 100 °C and atmospheric pressure, liquid water has a density of 958 kg m⁻³ and steam has a density of 0.598 kg m⁻³. What do these data show about the molecules in steam compared with those in the liquid water?

options.text: Their mean separation is about 12 times larger, as the volume per molecule is 1600 times larger.
Their mean separation is about 1600 times larger, because the density is 1600 times smaller.
Each molecule is about 1600 times larger, so each one takes up 1600 times the space.
Each molecule has about 1/1600 of the mass, because a gas is much lighter than a liquid.

questions.stem: Two solid cubes are cut from the same block of steel. Cube X has sides of length 2.0 cm and cube Y has sides of length 4.0 cm. Which statement correctly compares cube Y with cube X?

options.text: Y has eight times the mass of X and the same density as X.
Y has twice the mass of X and the same density as X.
Y has four times the mass of X and the same density as X.
Y has a greater density than X, because it contains more steel.

questions.explanation: Density is a property of the material, so both cubes have the density of steel. Volume scales as the cube of the length ratio: V_Y = (4.0/2.0)³ V_X = 8 V_X, and since m = ρV the mass is also eight times larger.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Kelvin and Celsius temperature scales is correct?

options.text: A Kelvin temperature is converted to degrees Celsius by adding 273, since both directions use the same rule.
A temperature has the same numerical value on both scales, as the kelvin is the SI name for the degree Celsius.
A Celsius temperature is converted to kelvin by adding 273, whether the Celsius value is above or below zero.
A temperature below the freezing point of water is negative on the Kelvin scale, exactly as it is on the Celsius scale.

questions.explanation: T/K = t/°C + 273 for every temperature. The two scales have divisions of the same size and differ only in their zero, which is 273 °C lower on the Kelvin scale, so −78 °C is 195 K and 27 °C is 300 K.

questions.stem: A mechanic tightens a nut with a spanner. She applies a force of 45 N to the handle at a point 0.30 m from the axis of the nut. The force makes an angle of 70° with the line joining the axis to the point where the force is applied. What is the magnitude of the torque of this force about the axis?
questions.explanation: τ = Fr sin θ, where θ is the angle between the force and the line from the axis to the point of application: τ = 45 × 0.30 × sin 70° = 13.5 × 0.940 = 12.7 N m.

questions.stem: A uniform plank of length 4.0 m and weight 150 N rests on a pivot 1.2 m from end A. A load of weight 90 N hangs from the other end, B. The weight of the plank acts at its midpoint. What weight must hang from end A for the plank to rest horizontally in equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Take torques about the pivot. The plank's weight acts 0.80 m from the pivot on the B side and the load at B is 2.8 m from it: 150 × 0.80 + 90 × 2.8 = 372 N m in one sense. W × 1.2 = 372, so W = 310 N.

questions.stem: A uniform bar lies at rest on frictionless horizontal ice. Two horizontal forces of equal, constant magnitude are then applied, one at each end of the bar, in opposite directions; each force is kept perpendicular to the bar at all times. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the bar while the forces act is correct?

options.text: It stays at rest and does not turn.
It rotates at a constant angular speed.

questions.stem: A bicycle travels along a level road at a constant 7.0 m s⁻¹. Its wheels, each of diameter 0.70 m, roll without slipping. What is the angular speed of each wheel?
questions.explanation: For rolling without slipping v = ωr, with r = 0.70/2 = 0.35 m. ω = v/r = 7.0/0.35 = 20.0 rad s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A flywheel rotating at 1500 revolutions per minute is brought to rest with uniform angular deceleration in 20 s. Through what angular displacement does it turn while stopping? (1 revolution = 2π rad.)

A thin hoop and a uniform solid disc have the same mass and the same radius. Each rotates about an axis through its centre, perpendicular to its plane. Which has the greater moment of inertia about this axis?

options.text: Neither, because bodies of equal mass have equal moments of inertia.
The hoop, as all its mass is at the maximum distance from the axis.
The disc, since its mass is spread out over its whole area.
Whichever of the two is rotating at the greater angular speed.

questions.explanation: Moment of inertia depends on how far the mass is from the axis. All of the hoop's mass is at distance R (I = MR²); much of the disc's mass is nearer the axis (I = ½MR²).
